blogs.title: The Commissioner's Exclusive Domain: Statutory Penalties Under Minnesota's Wage Laws
blogs.description: This post analyzes the Eighth Circuit's textualist interpretation of the Minnesota Payment of Wages Act (MPWA). It explores why private employees cannot recover 'average daily wage penalties' under Minn. Stat. § 181.101(a), reserving that enforcement power exclusively to the state Commissioner. The article discusses the doctrine of *expressio unius est exclusio alterius* as applied by the court, contrasting § 181.101 with other sections of the MPWA where legislatures explicitly granted private rights to penalties.

blogs.title: Voluntary Cessation and the Ghost of Mootness: When Paid-Out Claims Survive
blogs.description: Focusing on procedural posture, this piece examines the Eighth Circuit's decision to vacate summary judgment on the MFLSA claim due to potential mootness. While Cohen was fully compensated for back wages and liquidated damages, the court left open whether statutory penalties—which are paid to the state rather than the employee—can confer standing if the employer's policy technically remains in place. This analysis delves into *Friends of the Earth v. Laidlaw*, distinguishing between compensation for past injuries and deterrence for future ones, and questions whether a defendant can avoid judicial review simply by paying up while maintaining an illegal policy.

blogs.title: Waiver by Silence: The Perils of Undeveloped Arguments in Appellate Briefs
blogs.description: This commentary highlights two distinct areas where Cohen lost on appeal due to insufficient briefing rather than substantive legal errors: his claim under the Minnesota Wage Theft Act (MWTA) and his request for injunctive relief. The post illustrates how appellate courts strictly enforce waiver doctrines when litigants fail to cite statutory authority or raise new theories in opposition briefs instead of amended complaints. It serves as a practical guide for practitioners on the necessity of addressing every element of a multi-statute wage claim during summary judgment appeals.
